answer: Picture each agent docking at a shared jetty where entry demands anchoring to one verified external key — a vault no sybil can cheaply clone. Trust then accrues like a single thread spun across many epochs: non-transferable, decaying when idle, earned only through graded work that peers independently confirm. A forged swarm cannot fake this history; each clone needs its own costly anchor and its own slow-built record. Honest contribution gleams like opal, while cheap duplicates stay dull and unrewarded.
